body:
MEASURED 2026-08-11. vitest.config.mjs sets testTimeout: 20_000 and hookTimeout: 20_000. Its comment states why: the suite drives real sqlite files, and an fsync/WAL cycle on a loaded Windows runner legitimately costs seconds. That 20s is the platform-informed budget for this repo.

THE DEFECT: 32 test files call `vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: 15000 })` and pull themselves BELOW that default. Every one of the 32 sets exactly 15000. None of them sets hookTimeout, so each file already runs its hooks at 20s while capping its tests at 15s — the override is not a considered budget, it is a copied line that predates the config default.

The 32 do not fail together. They take turns, because which one breaches depends on which one the runner happens to load. Two observed breaches:
  (a) test/store/archive.test.ts — measured 20.1s against its own 15s ceiling, with the Defender exclusion from #359 confirmed applied.
  (b) test/cli/path-resolution.test.ts — timed out at 15s on PR #363.

THIS IS NOT #357, AND THE DISTINCTION IS LOAD-BEARING. PR #357 asked to RAISE archive.test.ts's budget above the repo default to accommodate a genuinely slow fixture. Myk closed it and asked for the root cause. That was right, and the root cause was found: T155 replaced 200 serialized fsyncs with a bounded pool, #359 added the Defender exclusion, and the file fell from 12-14s to 4.5s on Windows. THIS ticket raises no budget above the default. It stops 32 files from lowering themselves BELOW a default that was chosen for their platform. The ceiling those files land on is the one every other test file in the repo already runs under. No file gets more room than the repo grants by default; 32 files stop getting less.

VERIFIED, not assumed: no file among the 32 depends on the shorter budget. No test in them asserts that a timeout FIRES. The three files that manipulate time do it with their own inline budgets — erase-inmemory-reach.test.ts races a 1000ms setTimeout, subscribe.test.ts passes its own ms to a silence probe, dynamic-mounts.test.ts uses a 100ms inline argument — and none of the three reads the file-level value. serve-host.test.ts mentions a 10s timeout in a comment; that is a socket connect timeout in node's own stack, which its bindability probe exists to avoid paying. Exclusions: none. All 32 move.

THE FIX: substitute `vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: 15000 });` for `vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: 20_000 });` in all 32 files. Trailing comments on the line are preserved. 19 of the 32 are FROZEN rails, so the edit needs a scoped entry in scripts/rail-renames.json first — one entry, one substitution, 19 files, landed as its own PR because a branch cannot self-authorize.

THE RAIL, and it is the point: a new test asserts that NO test file sets a testTimeout below vitest.config.mjs's own default. It reads the default from the config rather than hardcoding it, so the floor follows the config if the config ever moves. Without that rail this ticket fixes 32 instances of a class and leaves the class open — the next copied line reopens it silently, because a lowered budget is invisible until a loaded runner picks that file.

NOT IN SCOPE: the files that set a budget ABOVE 20s (25000, 30000, 60000, 90_000, 120_000). Those are deliberate raises for browser drives, esbuild bundles and real scrypt work. They are above the default, not below it, and the rail permits them.

WHO MERGES: self-merge on the ordinary bar. Nothing the system promises changes. No assertion is touched. The fix moves a wall-clock ceiling up to the repo's own default and adds a rail that keeps it there.
title: 32 test files lower testTimeout BELOW the platform-informed default — a class of Windows CI flakes that takes turns picking a file
